bohemian-rhapsody-2018.gazette: Queen played Wembley Stadium on 13 July 1985, a Live Aid set of barely more than twenty minutes that is still cited as the day's high point. Freddie Mercury made his diagnosis public in a written statement on 23 November 1991, the day before he died. The film moves that knowledge back six years and puts it in the band's hands before they walk out to the piano.

custody-2018.gazette: The first long stretch of Custody takes place inside a family court hearing, two lawyers reading competing accounts while a judge decides on paper what a child's fortnight will look like. Xavier Legrand had already filmed this family once, in a 2013 short, and picks them up at the ruling. What follows is handovers, a withheld address, a phone passed between rooms — the machinery of shared custody working exactly as designed.

first-man-2018.gazette: James R. Hansen's authorized biography supplied the film's checklists and callouts, down to the program alarms that nearly aborted the lunar descent. It also supplied Karen Armstrong, dead of a brain tumour in 1962 at the age of two, a loss her father almost never discussed in public. The bracelet dropped into a crater on the Moon is the film's own invention; the record neither confirms it nor rules it out.
first-man-2018.prism: An authorized biography buys accuracy in the hardware and then spends it on the interior, which is the one place no source can be checked. The film is scrupulous about everything NASA logged and free with the part only Armstrong could have known.

free-solo-2018.gazette: On 3 June 2017 Alex Honnold climbed Freerider on El Capitan without a rope — some three thousand feet, in under four hours — with Jimmy Chin's crew rigged on the wall around him. The film also puts Honnold in an fMRI scanner and reports an amygdala that barely responds to images built to provoke it. Both the climb and the scan are entered as evidence, and the camera crew's own presence is entered alongside them.

green-book-2018.gazette: Victor Hugo Green's motorist guide ran from 1936 to 1966, listing the hotels, garages and lunch counters that would serve Black travellers in a country where most would not. The film builds a 1962 concert tour, and a friendship, on top of that document. Don Shirley's surviving relatives went on record after release to say the friendship was not one he claimed, and that no one had asked them.

leave-no-trace-2018.gazette: Granik shot in Forest Park and the timber country south of Portland, filling the edges of the frame with people already living the life the story describes — veterans, off-grid households, workers who were doing the work before the camera arrived. The plot comes from Peter Rock's novel, which started from a 2004 case: a veteran and his young daughter found living in that same park. The film's smallest parts are played by the people the film is about.
leave-no-trace-2018.prism: Casting the actual community makes the realism hard to argue with — you can't accuse a film of inventing a world its extras go home to. The cost is that those lives get borrowed to authenticate a story that isn't theirs.

mid90s-2018.gazette: The stock is 16mm and the frame is 4:3, the format the home skate videos of the period were actually shot in. Most of the crew surrounding the lead — Na-kel Smith, Olan Prenatt, Ryder McLaughlin — were cast off boards rather than out of auditions. The tricks in the film are theirs.

shadow-2018.gazette: Zhang Yimou's crew built the monochrome on the floor rather than in the grade: sets, armour and silk were painted in ink-wash greys so the palette existed before the camera saw it. What keeps its colour is skin, blood and wood. The technique is the film's argument about itself, made in the props department.

shoplifters-2018.gazette: Kore-eda has said the film began with Japanese news reports of households that went on collecting a dead relative's pension by never reporting the death — a run of cases that reached the national press in the years before he wrote it. He builds the family around that scandal rather than against it: shared meals, croquettes, a body under the floor, a wage made of small thefts. The Cannes jury gave it the Palme d'Or in May 2018.
shoplifters-2018.prism: The unsentimental eye cuts both ways — it makes the family lovable and keeps the fraud in the same frame, so affection never converts into acquittal. That refusal is what a lot of viewers read as endorsement.

sir-2018.gazette: Rohena Gera's film stays inside the geography of a Mumbai high-rise: the maid's room off the kitchen, the separate plate and cup, the service lift domestic workers are expected to take. Ratna was widowed young, which in her village closes nearly every door, and lives in as a servant in the city, which opens one narrow one. The arrangement is recorded rather than dramatised.

the-favourite-2018.gazette: Anne was pregnant seventeen times and outlived every child. Sarah Churchill ran her household and a good deal of her government until Abigail Masham displaced her, and was dismissed from court in 1711. The rumour about what happened in the bedchamber is itself part of the record — Sarah put it into circulation, in pamphlets, after she had already lost; Lanthimos takes a defeated courtier's accusation and shoots it as fact.

three-identical-strangers-2018.gazette: Three nineteen-year-olds found one another in 1980 and learned they had been placed with three different New York families on purpose, by one adoption agency, without their parents being told what they were part of. Peter Neubauer's study of the separated siblings was never published; the records went to Yale under seal until 2065. The film obtains a partial, redacted release and reads what it is given.
three-identical-strangers-2018.prism: A study that was never published still produced a result: three lives run as arms of an experiment nobody consented to. The sealing date does most of the work here — by 2065 everyone who could be embarrassed by the files, and everyone owed them, will be gone.

vice-2018.gazette: McKay opens with a title card conceding that Dick Cheney is among the most secretive leaders in modern history and that what follows was assembled from whatever could be found. The film then narrates itself: a bystander voice, a false ending rolled out halfway through, footnotes staged as scenes. Its claim to the record and its doubt about that claim are printed on the same frames.

won-t-you-be-my-neighbor-2018.gazette: In May 1969 Fred Rogers sat before a Senate subcommittee and talked a sceptical chairman into preserving twenty million dollars for public broadcasting; Morgan Neville lets the tape run. The archive carries most of the film — Officer Clemmons and the paddling pool, the week the programme took on assassination, thirty-three years of a show made deliberately slow. Neville goes looking for the gap between the man and the broadcast and turns up very little.

a-hidden-life-2019.gazette: Franz Jägerstätter was beheaded at Brandenburg-Görden on 9 August 1943 for refusing the oath to Hitler, a refusal his priest, his bishop and most of St. Radegund considered futile. The letters he and Franziska exchanged while he was held survived, were published, and supply a great deal of what the film's characters say aloud. Rome beatified him in 2007; Franziska, who lived to a hundred, was in the cathedral.
a-hidden-life-2019.prism: The film's authority rests on paper that exists only because the state let a condemned man write and a widow kept the letters for seventy years. Recognition arrived in 2007, which gave the village that shunned her most of a lifetime to be wrong in private.
